prompt: What types of guardrails should you implement to prevent exposure of personally identifiable information (PII) during both generation and memory storage? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Argument validation before calling payment APIs.
Regex or classifier-based filters on model outputs.
Blocking all access to user data completely.
Masking or redacting sensitive fields before storing in memory.
Use of rate-limiting to restrict tool usage frequency.

explanation: To prevent PII exposure, systems must actively filter/redact model outputs using regex or NLP classifiers and mask sensitive personal data before persisting records into long-term memory.

prompt: Match each production failure scenario to its corresponding guardrail defense:

pairs.left: Agent generates an invoice note containing racial slurs
Agent forgets to include mandatory legal disclaimer in email
Agent repeatedly loops and reschedules the same payment
Agent retrieves another client's confidential financial data
Agent produces vague, unsubstantiated summary of technical doc

explanation: Each failure mode aligns with a specific safeguard: slurs trigger moderation; missing disclaimers trigger output validation; rapid loops hit tool rate limits; unauthorized data hits PII filters; and hallucinations fail contextual grounding.

prompt: An architect proposes: 'Our autonomous agent executes wire transfers up to $500,000 completely without human review because we have an audit log written to disk every night.' What is the critical safety flaw?

options.text: High-stakes, irreversible financial actions require Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) approval gates before execution, not just retrospective HATL auditing after funds have already left.
Agents are never allowed to write audit logs to disk.
The agent should execute transfers using SMS messages instead.

explanation: Retrospective auditing (HATL) cannot recover funds once an irreversible $500,000 transaction has settled. High-stakes actions demand proactive Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) approval gates before execution occurs.
